episode.title: Positions and order
episode.teaching:
A number line is a map with one agreed direction. Values increase as you move right and decrease as you move left. Zero is a reference point. Positive numbers lie to its right and negative numbers to its left. The minus sign describes a position relative to zero; it does not mean a number is missing or invalid.

Imagine these equally spaced marks: **-3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3**. Moving one interval right changes the value by one. The point -1 is to the right of -3, so -1 is the greater number. Although the digit 3 is larger than the digit 1, the complete signed numbers have the opposite order. Read the sign together with the digit.

Spacing carries information. If adjacent labeled marks are 0 and 2, the interval represents two units, not one. For equally spaced marks **-4, -2, [blank], 2**, the blank is zero. Check the same interval on both sides before filling a missing label. A drawing can be wide or narrow without changing the values it represents.

Try a position check before looking at a result. On marks **-6, -3, 0, 3**, what does one interval represent? It represents three units. A point one interval right of zero is therefore 3. Count intervals, not the number of printed labels: two neighboring labels have one interval between them.

Now separate order from distance. The point -5 is farther from zero than -2, yet -2 is the greater value because it is farther right. If a question asks which position is greater, do not answer the distance question instead. A useful explanation names the direction: “-2 is to the right of -5.”

For optional practice, draw a short line with zero near the middle, label a consistent scale, and place two negative numbers and one positive number. You can also describe the line entirely in words. The checks use new values: one asks you to read a scale, and another asks you to apply ordering in a different situation. A wrong first check leaves fresh questions available; correcting a question you have already seen is practice rather than new independent evidence.

objectives.description: Read an equally spaced number line and compare signed positions.

context.question: The lesson says -5 is farther from zero than -2. How do I actually work out the distance between two points?
